fields.statement: Verifier at 4ba849e (attempt 2): go test -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/session-run-usage-limit passes. Its fake claude writes 'Claude AI usage limit reached|<past reset>' on its first launch and finishes on the second. session run reports 'ended: the agent exited with code 0', and claude.log holds exactly one 'start --session-id <id>' and one 'resume --resume <id>' for the same stored session ID, so no second session starts. go test -race -count=20 of TestSessionRunStopsAgentOpenAtLimit, TestSessionRunFailsWhenPausesRunOut and TestSessionRunFreshSessionWhenTranscriptGone passes. These tests cover the review findings: an agent left open at its limit is killed by the transcript watcher and resumed, and running out of the 24 pauses fails the session with a StateError exit instead of passing. Decision usage-limit-detect-and-wait-answer answers the blocking question. Diff read: watchLimit polls the transcript past its pre-launch length and kills p, and the loop now records a failure at the cap. The first make check failed only in the test target right after the timing-budget output, a known timing-contention flake; a rerun passed clean (exit 0), and go test ./... passed.
